newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South Africa's all gold index ended at a four year low on Wednesday as bullion's slight rally on a surge in palladium and platinum prices failed.
Golds refused to follow bullion, remaining flat to negative in morning trade before slipping to new lows.
"Golds did not follow platinum. The feeling is they should test lower levels than higher," one dealer said.
Palladium and platinum prices rose in the morning on a wildcat strike at Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd which is affecting 15-20 percent of total output.
Industrial shares ended weak in negative sentiment compounded by a higher-than-expected April consumer price index figure of 9.9 percent year-on-year.

Dealers said futures trade nudged shares lower and there was little institutional activity. The market also refused to follow Wall Street's overnight strength and was dampened by its slightly weaker open on Wednesday.

"It is mostly futures driven. We don't see lots of natural business. The market is basically falling on its own weight. There is no buying support," Johan Marais, director at Societe General Frankel Pollack, told Reuters.
He said the recent spate of weak company results were taking their toll on the market and indications of an early interest rate cut would remove the stranglehold.
The market was seen slowly heading lower with an occasional bounce until a development on interest rate cuts.
The gold index ended 8.1 points down at 1,178.5 points, the industrial index lost 37.4 points to 8,281.9 points and the all-share index was off 24.5 points to 7,040.8 points.

The market would look to the money supply and credit extension figures due after close of business on Wednesday. GDP growth figures would also help assess the direction of interest rates, dealers said.

Platinum shares benefitted from a wildcat strike at Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd which fuelled a rally in platinum and palladium prices. Rusplats touched 71.25 rand before retreating back to 70.25 rand.
Potgietersrust touched 28.50 rand before moving to 27.90 rand, 90 cents up. Leplats gained eight cents to 290 cents.

Other shares that gained include Tigon which jumped 20 percent at one stage but ended 16 percent higher, or 110 cents, at 800 cents as it recovers from the knock it received after its suspension from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Teljoy rises 50 cents to 505 cents as players speculate on the unbundling of its holding company Servgro.
Servgro said on Wednesday it was heavily involved in the second phase of its unbundling which it expected to be completed in the second half of 1997. It finished up 12 cents at 780 cents.
Near-term share futures ended soft despite a firm Wall Street overnight. Gold contracts were also down as bullion failed to sustain its slight rally.
Dealers said there was little foreign, institutional or basket buying in the market. April money supply and credit extension figures would be keenly watched.
The all-share contract was last at 6,355/63 from 6,441, the industrial contract was at 7,963/70 from 8,092 and the gold contract was at 824/29 from 839.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
